$comment: Confetti DARK — the theme-specific half of the editorial-gray dark mode. The neutrals themselves live on the mode axis (tokens/modes/dark.json), because Confetti's dark IS the base dark. Two things belong here instead, because both concern the BRAND and would be wrong for another theme inheriting the mode. (1) ACCESSIBILITY EXCEPTION — brand-as-text: the brand red (#c40000) is far below AA as TEXT on the graphite surfaces, so text.accent, the ghost hover, and status.danger.text all lift to red.300 (#f04b3a), which clears AA on EVERY dark surface including `card`, the lightest one (4.56:1). They sit here rather than on the mode axis because a theme inheriting the dark mode may have far lighter surfaces — red.300 fails on both Adventure's and Neon's cards — so the mode keeps the paler red.200 and only Confetti takes the lift. red.300 used to fail there at 3.56:1 and the accent had to settle for red.200, a much paler salmon; taking the surfaces deep is what bought the more saturated red back. The primary BUTTON is deliberately not overridden — its white label on the #c40000 fill is 6.27:1, so the fill stays brand-exact. (2) The four confetti hues get their own dark-mode BOLD values (the X.500 step): the light-mode bolds are pastels tuned to carry ink on cream, and on a neutral gray page they go dusty and read as washed out rather than chosen. These sit here and NOT on the mode axis because accent.* are brand-kit inputs — putting them in modes/dark.json would repaint Adventure's and Neon's accents too. Emitted under [data-theme='confetti'][data-mode='dark'] (specificity 0,2,0 — beats both the theme block and the mode block).

text.comment: danger AS TEXT takes the same lift brand-as-text takes, for the same reason — and like it, only Confetti can afford it. The mode axis leaves this on red.200 for the themes with lighter surfaces.
